findings.criterion: clicking ANY session tile reliably opens a warm terminal
findings.message: The North Star explicitly mandates that 'clicking ANY session tile reliably opens a warm terminal'. Phase 3 introduces a 'Two-step tile affordance' where the first click only opens a passive warm view, requiring a second 'Resume live' click to actually spawn the terminal. This directly violates the single-click-to-terminal requirement.

findings.criterion: measured truth, not zero-by-omission
findings.message: Phase 7 specifies a live drift tripwire that uses 'report.warn (never red)' if sidecar parsing fails on real files. If the upstream provider changes their sidecar format, parsing will fail, and Anchor will silently record zero usage for all new sessions while the pipeline remains 'green'. This directly violates 'not zero-by-omission' by allowing silent omission.

findings.criterion: clicking ANY session tile reliably opens a warm terminal
findings.message: Phase 6 introduces 'oldest-first graceful eviction' for parked worktrees, but fails to define how clicking an evicted session's tile will 'reliably open a warm terminal'. If the underlying worktree is deleted, the plan lacks a mechanism to reconstruct the PTY state and narrate the session, risking a broken or blank terminal upon click.

findings.criterion: Every Anchor session — interactive ConPTY or one-shot job... clicking ANY session tile reliably opens a warm terminal
findings.message: The North Star requires both 'interactive ConPTY' and 'one-shot job' sessions to reliably open a warm terminal on tile click. While Phase 4 captures cost for one-shot jobs, Phase 6's Playwright screenshot sign-off completely omits one-shot jobs from the tile classes it tests, leaving the terminal requirement unverified for these sessions.

The plan explicitly defers Gemini usage capture to a fast-follow. While multi-model support is desirable for future-proofing, the North Star does not mandate specific backend engines, only that the sessions that do run leave an honest trail. This is a known, documented deferral.

findings.criterion: clicking ANY session tile reliably opens a warm terminal that narrates what was done...
findings.section: Phase 3 — Phase 2 — Narration Backfill + Passive Warm Tile View
findings.message: The North Star explicitly promises that 'clicking ANY session tile reliably opens a warm terminal.' Phase 3 directly violates this by introducing a two-step affordance where the initial click only opens a 'PASSIVE warm view (no PTY)' and requires a separate 'Resume live' click to actually spawn the terminal. You are breaking the core UX contract to avoid spawning a PTY.

findings.criterion: Every Anchor session — interactive ConPTY or one-shot job — leaves an honest, machine-verified trail of what it cost... not zero-by-omission
findings.message: By explicitly deferring Gemini segment capture and relying on an 'unmeasured' badge, the plan fails the 'Every Anchor session' mandate. Rebranding a missing cost as 'unmeasured' is exactly 'zero-by-omission' disguised as transparency. A competitor would rightly point out that the rollup numbers are still fundamentally incomplete if a major engine's costs are ignored.

findings.criterion: narrates what was done, what was produced, and what comes next
findings.section: Phase 3 — Phase 2 — Narration Backfill + Passive Warm Tile View
findings.message: The 'Substantive degraded seed' fallback just dumps a doc list, dates, and a transcript tail. This completely fails the North Star promise to narrate 'what was done, what was produced, and what comes next'. Providing a raw data dump when a summary is missing is not a narration, and it breaks the guaranteed orientation UX for those sessions.

Implementing a bounded parked-worktree budget and oldest-first eviction logic is entirely unrelated to cost capture or reliable session resume. This is a disk-space management feature smuggled into the plan. Remove it to keep the project strictly focused on the North Star.

findings.criterion: Honesty contract holds and is test-pinned
findings.message: Phase 7 mandates reporting on historical cost backfill ('attributed / surviving / total' based on sidecars), but Phase 4 explicitly defers all retroactive cost attribution, asserting pre-feature sessions will simply surface as 'unmeasured'. You cannot deploy and report on a backfill process that was explicitly deferred. Reconcile this contradiction.

findings.criterion: Resume narrates and orients
findings.message: Running a one-time batch summary backfill using model calls (runner seam) across all brownfield and pre-v7 sessions introduces massive API costs and execution time for purely cosmetic reasons. Since Phase 3 already defines a 'substantive degraded seed' (pure render of doc list + transcript tail) that ensures the window is never blank, the active backfill is unnecessary overhead. Rely on the degraded seed for historical sessions and drop the batch API jobs.

findings.criterion: The diag-B2 tile inconsistencies are REPRODUCED
findings.message: Building a dedicated 'anonymized fixture capture tool' dev command is heavy tooling for an issue that likely only requires manually copying a broken project folder to the fixture directory. Do not over-engineer the reproduction step when a simple cp command suffices.
